profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged StreamData Center, sits on West Creek Lane in Chaska, Minnesota, part of the Minneapolis metro area. Stream own site describes two adjacent buildings on this street that could not be disambiguated from the coordinates alone this session: Minneapolis I at 1708 West Creek Lane, a 7.2 megawatt, 75,800 square foot facility opened in June 2014 that Stream own site states was sold in January 2024 to a colocation provider, and Minneapolis II, also known internally as MSPA1, at 1706 West Creek Lane, a 2.4 megawatt facility expandable by another 2.4 megawatts across 56,000 square feet split into two 10,000 square foot data halls, opened in December 2017 and, per Stream own site, fully leased to an unnamed large commercial bank and still Stream-operated. Because both buildings sit on the same short street and this record generic naming does not specify which one it represents, no single capacity or square footage figure is assigned to it individually, though both real, sourced figures are presented here for context rather than omitted or averaged into an invented composite number. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem, marketing a wholesale and build-to-suit model with more than 90 percent of capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers. Chaska sits within Carver County, a fast-growing exurb southwest of downtown Minneapolis, and Stream decision to develop two separate buildings on the same short street over a roughly three-year span reflects the broader Minneapolis market steady demand growth through the mid-2010s, well before the market later cooled enough for Stream to sell the earlier of the two buildings in 2024.
profile.research_note: Two adjacent Stream buildings on West Creek Lane could not be matched to this record specific coordinates this session. Minneapolis I (7.2MW/75,800sqft/2014/sold Jan 2024) and Minneapolis II/MSPA1 (2.4MW+2.4MW expandable/56,000sqft/2017/fully leased to unnamed bank/still Stream-operated) figures both from Stream own site, presented without picking one arbitrarily.

reading.body:
This registry row represents a campus in Chaska, Minnesota that comprises two adjacent buildings on West Creek Lane, one still operated by Stream and one sold to LightEdge in January 2024. The research notes describe the ambiguity precisely: the row's generic coordinates and address do not specify which building it represents, and resolving that ambiguity requires parcel-level geocoding or re-verification of the operator field itself. Until that resolution, this row cannot be confidently attributed to either Stream or LightEdge, and cannot be matched to a specific published capacity figure.

The state context shows Minnesota has 13 mapped data center facilities and only 2 with published capacity figures totaling 10 MW. This row ranks third in the state by published megawatts, but that ranking applies only if the row's specifications are correct and unambiguous. The state context does not clarify what published power specifications this row itself carries, and the ambiguity over which building it represents means no capacity figure can be safely attributed to either operator at this location.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI, the material fact is the unresolved identity of the facility. The research status is marked complete, but completion here means documenting a genuine ambiguity rather than resolving it. Until the specific building and its current operator are confirmed through parcel-level geocoding or direct re-verification, this row cannot inform decisions about either Stream's capacity in Minnesota or LightEdge's footprint. A future researcher should treat this as a flagged case requiring ground-truth verification before it can be read as a published specification.
